17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 24 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as two packages that work together: 25 26 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 27 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 28 29 ### Short Answer 30 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 31 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 32 33 ### Why Keep Both? 34 - Independent versioning and stability 35 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 36 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 37 - Reuse across surfaces 38 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 39 - Smaller, focused installs 40 - Operators install the CLI. 41 - Builders install only the core library they need. 42 43 ### When to Use Each 44 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 45 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 46 47 ### Concrete Examples 48 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 49 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 50 51 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 52 53 --- 54 55 ## Getting Started with the CLI 56 57 1. Install the published CLI: 58 ```bash 59 npm install -g frai 60 ``` 61 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 62 ```bash 63 frai --setup 64 ``` 65 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 66 3. Run the interactive workflow: 67 ```bash 68 frai 69 ``` 70 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 71 72 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 73 74 --- 75 76 ## CLI Command Reference 77 78 | Command | Purpose | 79 |---------|---------| 80 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 81 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 82 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 83 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 84 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 85 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 86 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 87 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 88 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 89 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 90 91 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 92 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 93 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 94 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 95 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 96 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 97 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 98 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 99 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 100 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 101 102 ### `frai generate [options]` 103 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 104 105 ### `frai scan` 106 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 107 108 ### `frai setup` 109 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 110 111 ### `frai config` 112 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 113 114 ### `frai docs` 115 Utilities for generated artefacts: 116 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 117 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 118 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 119 120 ### `frai rag index [options]` 121 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 122 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 123 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 124 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 125 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 126 127 ### `frai eval` 128 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 129 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 130 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 131 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 132 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). 179 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 180 ``` 181 182 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 183 184 --- 185 186 ## Local Development 187 188 Clone the repository and work from source: 189 ```bash 190 pnpm install 191 pnpm --filter frai run build 192 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 193 ``` 194 195 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 196 ```bash 197 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 198 # then 199 frai --setup 200 ``` 201 202 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 203 204 --- 205 206 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 207 208 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 209 210 1. 1	# Responsible AI Gate - Design
2	
3	*Date: 2026-08-05 · Status: implemented*
4	
5	## What this adds
6	
7	Inspired by [addyosmani/agent-skills](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills) - a collection of
8	engineering skills that force AI coding agents through quality gates (spec → plan → build → verify) -
9	FRAI gains the **responsible-AI equivalent of that gate**, without replicating the generic lifecycle
10	skills. One gate, done deeply:
11	
12	> **No AI feature spec is complete without a Responsible AI Gate section, and nothing ships
13	> until the gate passes.**
14	
15	Three pieces:
16	
17	| Piece | Path | What it is |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| Skill | [sebuzdugan/frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) (moved out of this repo 2026-08-05) | An agent skill (agent-skills `SKILL.md` format, installable via `npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai`) that makes any coding agent write specs that include the RAI Gate |
20	| Spec template | `packages/frai-gate/assets/rai-spec-template.md` (canonical copy also in frai-skills) | Copy-paste spec template with the `## Responsible AI Gate` section built in |
21	| Pipeline | `packages/frai-gate/` | `frai-gate` - a Claude Agent SDK pipeline + deterministic validator that drafts, checks, and enforces the gate (CI-friendly) |
22	
23	## The gate: seven checks
24	
25	Aligned with frai-core's questionnaire dimensions (core / impact / data / performance / monitoring / bias)
26	plus the EU AI Act tiering already used by FRAI Chat:
27	
28	1. **Risk tier** - EU AI Act-aligned classification (prohibited / high / limited / minimal) with justification. High-risk requires a named human sign-off.
29	2. **Data provenance & privacy** - sources, PII handling, consent basis, retention.
30	3. **Human oversight** - automation level, override path, kill switch.
31	4. **Evaluation plan** - pre-ship metrics with numeric thresholds.
32	5. **Bias & fairness** - affected groups, mitigations, how tested.
33	6. **Monitoring & rollback** - production monitoring, degradation detection, rollback trigger.
34	7. **Transparency & incident response** - user disclosure of AI, incident owner and process.
35	
36	Verdicts: **PASS** (all checks complete) / **WARN** (complete but weak answers) / **BLOCK**
37	(missing sections, placeholders, or high-risk without sign-off). BLOCK exits non-zero for CI.
38	
39	## frai-gate pipeline (Claude Agent SDK)
40	
41	Two layers so it is useful with or without an API key:
42	
43	- **Deterministic layer (no key needed):** parses the spec markdown, verifies every gate
44	  subsection exists and is answered (no `TBD`/placeholder text), enforces the high-risk
45	  sign-off rule. Powers `frai-gate check` and CI.
46	- **Smart layer (Claude Agent SDK):** `query()` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` with
47	  read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) scoped to the repo:
48	  - `frai-gate draft` - scans the codebase for AI indicators, then drafts a filled-in
49	    RAI Gate section grounded in what the code actually does.
50	  - `frai-gate check --smart` - after the deterministic pass, adversarially reviews each
51	    gate answer for quality (vague thresholds, untestable claims) and adds findings.
52	
53	Commands: `frai-gate init` (drop the template into the repo) · `frai-gate check <spec>` ·
54	`frai-gate draft [--out <file>]` · all support `--json`.
55	
56	## Decisions
57	
58	- **TypeScript package mirroring `frai-agent`** (tsc build, `dist/`, ESM) - matches monorepo conventions.
59	- **Claude Agent SDK, not LangChain** - the user asked for an Agent SDK pipeline; `frai-agent`
60	  (LangChain/OpenAI) stays untouched. The SDK's built-in Read/Glob/Grep tools replace custom scan
61	  plumbing, with `permissionMode` restricted and write tools disallowed.
62	- **Skill lives in `skills/`** at repo root so the standard `npx skills add` layout finds it, and
63	  a `/rai-spec` slash command is provided under `.claude/commands/` for Claude Code users.
64	- **Only one skill** - deliberately no spec/plan/build/test clones; agent-skills already covers those.

1	# frai-gate
2	
3	The **FRAI Gate** (Responsible AI Gate) for specs - part of [FRAI](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai).
4	
5	Every spec for an AI-touching feature must contain a complete `## FRAI Gate`
6	section - seven checks - and implementation doesn't start until the gate passes:
7	
8	1. Risk tier (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk requires a named human sign-off)
9	2. Data provenance & privacy
10	3. Human oversight
11	4. Evaluation plan (numeric thresholds)
12	5. Bias & fairness
13	6. Monitoring & rollback
14	7. Transparency & incident response
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```bash
19	npx frai-gate init --ci                 # scaffold FRAI-SPEC.md + a GitHub Action that runs
20	                                        # the gate on every PR (works in any repo)
21	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md         # deterministic validation - no API key needed
22	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # + adversarial AI review of answer quality
23	npx frai-gate draft                     # read-only agent scans the repo and drafts a
24	                                        # gate section grounded in your actual code
25	```
26	
27	Also available as `frai gate ...` from the main [frai CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai).
28	
29	Exit codes: `0` PASS/WARN · `1` BLOCK · `2` usage/error - drop `frai-gate check` straight into CI.
30	
31	`draft` and `--smart` run on the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk)
32	with read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) and need Claude Code authentication or
33	`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Override the model with `FRAI_GATE_MODEL` (default `claude-opus-5`).
34	
35	> **Privacy note:** `draft` and `--smart` send the repository content the agent reads to

# Plan: Fix `frai gate init --ci` Flag Passing

## Context
The `frai` CLI doesn't pass the `--ci` flag through to `frai-gate`, so `frai gate init --ci` creates the FRAI-SPEC.md file but fails to create `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`. Running `frai-gate init --ci` directly works correctly, confirming the issue is in how frai-cli delegates the command.

## Root Cause
In `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 738-755), the `gate` command:
1. Uses Commander.js with `.allowUnknownOption(true)` to pass arbitrary flags to frai-gate
2. Defines the command as `.command('gate [args...]')` to capture variadic arguments
3. Only passes the variadic `args` to the spawned frai-gate child process
4. Commander doesn't include unknown options (like `--ci`) in the variadic args array—they're stored separately in the command object but ignored

When a user runs `frai gate init --ci`, Commander parses:
- `args = ['init']` (variadic args)
- `--ci` as an unknown option (not included in args)
- Result: spawns `node frai-gate/dist/cli.js init` (missing `--ci`)

## Solution
Access the Commander command object to retrieve unknown options and combine them with variadic args before spawning frai-gate:

**File to modify:** `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 738-755, the `gate` command action handler)

**Change:**
1. Modify the action handler to receive the Commander command object as the second parameter: `.action(async (args: string[], cmd) => {`
2. Combine variadic args with unknown options from the command object
3. Pass the complete argument list to frai-gate

The frai-gate CLI's parseArgs() function manually parses arguments (packages/frai-gate/src/cli.ts, lines 52-72), so it will correctly handle any flag format passed to it.

## Implementation Details
- Access `cmd.opts()` to get known options
- Check for unknown options in the Commander command structure or use `process.argv` as a fallback
- Build the complete args array: `['init', '--ci']` instead of just `['init']`
- Spawn frai-gate with the complete argument list

## Verification
After rebuilding with `pnpm --filter frai build`:
1. Run: `node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js gate init --ci` from an empty folder
2. Verify both files are created:
   - `FRAI-SPEC.md` should exist
   - `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` should exist
3. Confirm the workflow file contains valid GitHub Actions YAML with the gate check command
